content.title: Virginia women's March Madness run ends as Cavaliers fall to TCU
content.text: Virginia women’s basketball saw its magical run in the NCAA Tournament end with a 79-69 loss to TCU in the Sweet 16 Saturday, March 28.After leading at halftime, Virginia (22-12) struggled in the third quarter, getting outscored 24-11. Virginia shot just 4-of-15 (26.7%) in the third after shooting 15-of-32 (46.9%) in the opening half. Marta Suarez scored 13 points for the Horned Frogs in the third quarter, part of a dominating 33-point, 10-rebound performance.AdvertisementOlivia Miles just missed a triple-double for TCU (32-5) with 28 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists.Virginia had its largest lead after Kymora Johnson hit a 3-pointer in the first quarter to put her team up 21-14. Johnson had eight points on 3-of-7 shooting in the first quarter but was just 4-of-15 the rest of the way. The sophomore, who was averaging 19.5 points a game coming into the day, finished with 18 points.Paris Clark left Virginia with 20 points in the loss.Mar 28, 2026; Sacramento, CA, USA; Virginia Cavaliers guard Paris Clark (1) pushes the ball up the court during the first quarter of the game against the Texas Christian University Horned Frogs in the Sweet Sixteen game of the Sacramento Regional 4 of the women's 2026 NCAA Tournament at Golden 1 Center. Mandatory Credit: Ed Szczepanski-Imagn ImagesVirginia trailed by as many as 15 in the fourth quarter before a furious rally cut its deficit to six with 27.1 seconds left, but the Cavaliers could get no closer. AdvertisementNo. 10-seed Virginia was the lowest seed remaining in the tournament after advancing to the Sweet 16 from the First Four, the first team to do that in the NCAA Women’s Tournament.Virginia beat Arizona State to open the tournament, then upset seventh-seeded Georgia before upsetting second-seeded Iowa in double-overtime. But it couldn’t keep the upsets coming against TCU.The Cavaliers advanced to the Sweet 16 for the first time since 2000 and were trying to advance to the Elite Eight for the first time since 1996.TCU will face top-seeded South Carolina March 30 for a chance to advance to the Final Four.AdvertisementMore: UNC basketball coaching search: Who should be next coach for Tar Heels?More: NC State basketball coaching candidates: 6 options to replace Will WadePatrick Hite is a reporter at The News Leader.
